pages.title: Fields → food, feed and animal care
pages.intro: Reserve seed before turning crops into food or feed. Art of Growing adds bundle processing; not all Livestock Welfare modules are enabled.

steps.label: Prepare a field
steps.text: Hoe suitable soil, provide water and protect crops from animals. Match crops to temperature and nutrient needs; rotate crops or replenish depleted nutrients.

steps.label: Dry the harvest
steps.text: Mature rye drops wet grain bundles under the installed crop patch. Shift-right-click bundles onto the ground and wait for them to dry.

steps.label: Thresh and allocate
steps.text: Use a stick on a placed dry bundle stack to separate grains from straw. Keep seeds for replanting. The knife-plus-rye-seed crafting recipe yields rye grain for the kitchen.

steps.label: Feed appropriately
steps.text: Stock a trough with species-appropriate feed. Art of Growing adds rye seeds to the large trough; this does not prove every animal accepts that feed.

steps.label: Maintain living conditions
steps.text: Welfare Hygiene, Weather and Thirst modules are enabled. Provide clean surroundings, weather protection and water; its Safety settings allow animal deaths. These are not decorative animal-care rules.

steps.label: Do not impose disabled breeding rules
steps.text: Breeding.Enabled is false. RequireBedding=true and pregnancy/portion values are inside that disabled module: do not teach them as active requirements. This does not establish that all breeding is disabled; Better Husbandry and GeneLib are installed too.

steps.label: Return nutrients
steps.text: Natural Fertilizer supplies manure slurry and compost barrel recipes. Follow their item recipes before applying fertilizer; an installed recipe does not prove every animal produces its ingredients.

unknowns: Manual Harvesting, Better Husbandry, GeneLib, Catch Livestock and DairyPlus DLL interactions are not live-tested; no fertility, capture or milk schedule is asserted.

pages.title: Carcass → kitchen, bones and leather
pages.intro: Process animals at the installed stations, then keep food handling separate from the hide barrel line.

steps.label: Bring the body home
steps.text: Right-click a supported dead animal to carry it in a free bag slot; small bodies fit ordinary inventory slots. Field harvesting sacrifices yield. FieldHarvestingLightMode is false.

steps.label: Skin and bleed
steps.text: Place the body on a skinning hook. Hold right-click with a knife to skin it; wait for its bled-out color before removing it. Work promptly because bodies rot on stations.

steps.label: Butcher and sort
steps.text: Put the bled-out body on a butchering table and process it with a knife or cleaver. Break the remaining bone carcass for bones. Send meat to cooking/preservation and skins to the appropriate hide recipes.

steps.label: Render fat
steps.text: The installed pot recipe uses two litres water and two raw primemeat to make one rendered fat. Its output is fat-rendered, not the generic fat link in the older guide prose.

steps.label: Soak and scrape
steps.text: Make limewater from lime and water. Seal a compatible raw hide in the limewater recipe. Craft the soaked hide with a knife in the grid to obtain scraped hide; species-specific recipes convert supported skins to size-based scraped hides.

steps.label: Tan twice
steps.text: Make weak tannin with oak or acacia logs and water; use another log with weak tannin for strong tannin. Seal scraped hide in weak tannin for 72 hours; then prepared hide in strong tannin for 108 hours. A small hide needs two litres per stage and yields one plain normal leather.

steps.label: Use leather
steps.text: Use plain normal leather in the relevant equipment recipe. Sewn body/leg armor also requires flax twine. Do not substitute pelts or arbitrary species skins for generic tanning ingredients.

unknowns: No universal conversion from every species skin to generic hide is asserted.
Carcass/station and animal-mod interactions were not executed.

pages.title: Bees → repeatable honey and wax
pages.intro: Keep a populated skep for transferring bees into reusable ceramic or Langstroth hives. The upgraded hives do not propagate like vanilla skeps.

steps.label: Establish bees
steps.text: Use the skep route to obtain a populated colony, then move it to a flower-rich apiary. Keep that occupied skep for populating upgraded hives.

steps.label: Build a ceramic hive
steps.text: Clay-form and fire a ceramic brood pot and hive top. Transfer the skep colony to the pot and attach the top. The hive retains its colony through the top-harvesting cycle. Interacting with the brood pot while holding the populated skep consumes the skep.

steps.label: Harvest and reset
steps.text: When the top is ready, remove it and use a knife to harvest the comb; replace the emptied top. Process comb for honey and wax without destroying the populated brood pot.

steps.label: Prepare Langstroth frames
steps.text: Build the base, supers, brood box and rack from the native Langstroth guide. Wax linen and cut it into frame liners; fit liners to empty frames on the rack before production.

steps.label: Assemble and repeat
steps.text: Put lined frames in supers, close them and stack them on the base; add the populated brood box on top. Harvest ready frames on the rack with a knife, repair as instructed, then return frames and hive parts.

steps.label: Integrate with fields
steps.text: The installed pollination guide describes benefits for nearby crops, berries and fruit trees. Use that native guide instead of assuming vanilla-only bee behavior or one universal effective radius.

unknowns: Honey yield, pollination reach, timing and frame wear are not live-tested.
Native Langstroth text contains inconsistent wax totals; no exact shopping list is repeated.

Native prose links to obsolete blue/gray ceramic codes; drafts instead use ashforest states actually declared in installed definitions. Duplicate fancy/new ceramic definitions require loader/runtime checking.

pages.title: Flax and fleece → cloth and clothes
pages.intro: Flax passes through bundle processing before spinning. Wool has a separate washable fleece line; cloth, twine and block linen are distinct materials.

steps.label: Dry and thresh flax
steps.text: Mature flax drops wet grain bundles. Place and dry them, then thresh the dry stack with a stick. Reserve the recovered flax seed; keep dry flax straw for fiber.

steps.label: Ret, rinse and soften
steps.text: Soak dry straw in fresh water. Rinse wet straw using the installed water-container or barrel recipe to obtain clean straw. Hold right-click with clean straw to crumple it, then process crumpled straw with a ridge in the offhand to separate fiber.

steps.label: Spin and weave linen
steps.text: Tailor’s Delight adds spindle-assisted flax twine. Four twine around a stick make plain cloth; plain cloth converts to a normal linen block and returns the stick. Respect any displayed class requirement.

steps.label: Shear and wash fleece
steps.text: The native guide requires living generation-one-or-higher animals and recommends shears; knives risk injury. Wash generic plain fleece with 0.5 litre limewater for 18 hours to obtain generic plain fibers. Species and colors are separate variants.

steps.label: Spin and weave wool
steps.text: Use the enabled spinning recipe; the installed Tailor’s Delight compatibility assets add spindle recipes. Wool twine plus a stick makes portable wool cloth; the square-twine recipe makes a wool block.

steps.label: Sew the selected garment
steps.text: Dressmakers recipes may require dyed cloth, leather bundles, colored twine and an awl. The pack enables common/class/Nadiyan clothing and wool alternatives; this is not removal of clothier trait gates.

unknowns: Conditional compatibility-folder loading and offhand processing need runtime validation.
Raw class-restricted recipes do not prove all-class crafting access.
